metas.name: Botswana - A20
metas.note: The A20 has mostly clean, recent asphalt. Some sections of the road are much thinner than usual. The landscape is characterised by red soil, dry grey-coloured trees, and very little grass
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - A20 - southeast of Tshabong
metas.note: Southeast of Tshabong, the A20 has been recently repainted and has very bright yellow lines and relatively dark asphalt. There is a powerline running alongside it to the northeast, it has orange-tan sandy soil, and you can often find patches of yellow flowers.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - A30
metas.note: This portion of the A30 has a distinct autumn feel unique to it. Notably, there are trees with orange coloured leaves lining the road in straight rows. In addition, there is often tall grass as opposed to other autumn looking locations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Chobe Flood Plains National Park
metas.note: Chobe Flood Plains National Park in the far north has a lot of small, winding dirt road coverage, with a lot of it being just south of the Chobe River. It has scattered lush bushes on either side, and you will often find wildlife such as elephants and warthogs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Extremely white sandy soil
metas.note: The mostly unpaved road north of Maun to Khwai can be identified by extremely white sandy soil and tall green trees surrounding the road. The first section of the road, between Maun and Shorobe, is paved. But that section can still be identified by the trees, faint road markings, and power lines to the west of the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Pandamatenga silos
metas.note: These distinctive silos are found in Pandamatenga in northeastern Botswana and can be seen all around the town.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Rural Gaborone
metas.note: Just outside Gaborone, there is a lot of coverage along very rural, small dirt tracks. They can be identified by the orange-red shade of dirt and abundance of green trees and bushes surrounding the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Salt pans
metas.note:
Salt pans can be found in central-eastern Botswana. Dirt road coverage can be found leading to the pans and has similar soil and grass, but you can also find many trees along the road. They are mainly found around the Nwetwe pan. The salt pans show up as lakes on the map.

NOTE: A lot of the dirt road coverage near the pans was taken in June, and will feature trees without leaves or those that are beginning to lose their leaves.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Section of the A33
metas.note:
The section of the A33 within the Sibuya Forest Reserve and the CT/3 (Tamafupa) Commercial Wildlife Utilisation is under construction. This is most visible by the service road or embankment alongside the road.

NOTE: Despite being in the construction zone, some locations may still look normal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Tsadilo Hills World Heritage Site
metas.note: The Tsodilo Hills World Heritage Site is memorable due to its large protruding hills with exposed rock faces. The coverage around the hills is entirely on dirt roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Botswana - Western part of the A2
metas.note: The western part of the A2 has overcast coverage, making it recognisable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/botswana.

metas.name: Eswatini - Dirt
metas.note: The MR3 South of Ngomane can be recognized thanks to flatness, long dry grass and the dirt on the camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - Diveded road
metas.note:
The MR3 from Manzini to the South African border is divided by metal and stone guardrails, making it recognisable.

HINT: This road is the only divided highway found in Eswatini.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - East ridge
metas.note: The MR8 in Southeastern Eswatini straddling the South African border is recognisable because of this distinct ridge to the east.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - Mlawula Nature Reserve
metas.note: You can recognise the Mlawula Nature Reserve thanks to the narrow dirt tracks, tall grass and overall savannah landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Eswatini - Portuguese
metas.note:
If you see Portuguese text in Eswatini, you are most likely in the small town of Lomahasha.

NOTE: This is because of its proximity to Mozambique, where Portuguese is spoken.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Ghana - "Reunion" car
metas.note: Several nature reserves and sanctuaries have this unique car. A white car and side mirrors will be visible instead of the regular car, however, the ‘Ghana tape’ will still be there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Ankasa car
metas.note: The Ankasa Game Reserve has a unique Google car. The entire front of the Google car can be seen, with only the actual camera blurred. The roof of the car will have a street view vinyl and the ‘Ghana tape’ will be present.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Boabeng Fiema Monkey Sanctuary
metas.note:
The Boabeng Fiema Monkey Sanctuary has a unique Google car. The ‘Ghana tape’ and roof rack will not be visible however, the black right side mirror will be slightly visible just outside the blur.

NOTE: The red soil and surrounding vegetation should still be good clues for the country, despite the lack of the typical car meta associated with Ghana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - East of Accra
metas.note: The coastal area just east of Accra, especially on the N1, has a distinct landscape: it is very flat and wide open, with significantly less vegetation than the rest of southern Ghana. Some parts can look somewhat dry.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Keta Lagoon
metas.note: The Keta Lagoon in the southeast of Ghana can be seen on the road that runs along it, with the lake being most visible in the northern section. You can sometimes see grey rocks on the side of the road. The soil is quite sandy in comparison to the rest of the country, and it should have a coastal feel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - N1 near the border town of Elubo
metas.note:
The section of the N1 road near the border town of Elubo is very new: it has dark and unblemished asphalt, a very crisp-looking middle line, and no outer lines. The vegetation is dense and occasionally features palm trees.

NOTE: This new road surface continues until the town of Azuleti. The middle line can be dashed or solid. Near Azuleti, the road does not have a middle line.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - N2 in Volta Region
metas.note: On a section of the N2 east of Lake Volta, you can often see a ridgeline to your southeast, somewhat close to the road. The road itself also has a distinct angle, running in a general SW-NE direction. The sky is very overcast and grey.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Nkwanta-Domanko road
metas.note:
The road between Nkwanta and Domanko is unpaved, with a powerline close to the road to your east or northeast. The road itself runs in a general SE-NW direction, through a lush savannah landscape that is typical of central Ghana.

NOTE: In urban areas, there can be a powerline on both sides of the road. In addition, a section of the Salaga-Tamale road has a powerline to the east as well, but the darker soil and moody cloud cover makes it distinguishable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - North of Wa
metas.note:
Most unpaved roads in a dry savannah landscape are found north of Wa, as well as near the town itself.

NOTE: The other unpaved roads in northern Ghana are the Yendi-Nkwanta road in the east, and part of the Salaga-Tamale road, which has very distinct soil. See the tips below.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Salaga-Tamale road
metas.note:
The Salaga-Tamale road up to Kpalbusi is a dirt road with very moody overcast coverage. The soil tends to be very dark, with a purple or brown tinge to it. The road also has a unique tropical savannah feel. The soil is most dark near the town of Salaga.

NOTE: Unpaved roads with overcast coverage and a savannah landscape can be found in other places. The unique aspect of this road is the dark purplish brown soil and the especially dark cloud cover.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Ghana - Sawla-Fulfoso road
metas.note:
The road connecting the town of Sawla with the N10 has very crisp, new road lines. Most of the road runs in a general east-west direction, through a lush savannah landscape. The middle line can be solid or dashed.

NOTE: There are a couple of other roads with crisp road lines like these, however these tend to have a different road angle or landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ghana.

metas.name: Kenya - A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit
metas.note: The A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit has many plants alongside the road and you will often see large mountains in the distance. The stretch going through Namunyak Wildlife Conservation Trust will have a very large mountain range to the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - A2 north of Marsabit
metas.note: A2 north of Marsabit will be much flatter, with some mountains in the distance. The stretch just north or Marsabit will have mountains visible to the south, while further north, a different range can be seen. It will also have much less vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - A3 north of Garissa
metas.note: The A3 north of Garissa is very unique, with light coloured soil and many green trees on either side of the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Aberdare National Park
metas.note: Aberdare National Park has a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. Almost all of the coverage is outside of the National Park, with only two roads within the park covered. The main road through the park has these rubber bands on the roof rack, which can only be found in one other National Park in Kenya.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Amboseli National Park
metas.note: Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - B9
metas.note: The B9 in the Northeast is entirely unpaved and has bright reddish orange dirt with many trees surrounding the road. Most of it is very flat, but the coverage at the western end of the road can have hills and mountains. The soil also transitions into a more sandy colour.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Dirt
metas.note: This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Homa Bay
metas.note: Homa Bay has this protruding hill to the east that is often visible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Kerio-Lodwar area
metas.note:
The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation.

You may also find yourself in Generation 3 coverage without car meta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Mara Triangle
metas.note: Mara Triangle has no considerable mountains and most of it is either flat or hilly. It has a white car that can be found in other Kenyan National Parks. Generation 4 coverage exists there as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Mt Kilimanjaro
metas.note:
In a lot of the coverage north of Mt Kilimanjaro, the mountain is visible to the south, usually obscured by clouds. In the city of Oloitoktok, the mountain will often be visible directly to the south.

NOTE: The map shows the location of Mt Kilimanjaro, but it can be seen from very far away.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Nairobi
metas.note: Nairobi is the largest city in the country, and capital of Kenya. It is the only city to have a considerable amount of skyscrapers, and is highly developed. It is densely populated, and is surrounded by small, poor settlements.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Rubber bands
metas.note: Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, you can find the Aberdare car as well, but it will always have rubber bands, unlike in Aberdare where it will only have them on the main roads through the park. It can be differentiated from Aberdare by its redder dirt, and greener landscape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Succulents
metas.note: This stretch of the B8 just north of Kibaoni has many succulents on the side of the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Kenya - Western part of the C34
metas.note: The western part of the C34 is a flat, east to west road. There are two long, straight sections with an abundance of sugar cane. Furthermore, you will see a large mountain range north along the entire mentioned stretches of road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kenya.

metas.name: Lesotho - A5 Bollard
metas.note:
Several sections of the A5 south of Nyakosoba are under construction. As a result, you will often see a sort of temporary “bollard” next to the road, consisting of a stick that is mostly painted white.

Even on sections without the bollard, you can often recognize this road, as it is a wide dirt road with very dark brown soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Maseru
metas.note:
The only city with a significantly urbanised downtown area is Maseru, the capital. All other towns have a very provincial feel in comparison to Maseru.

Note that the suburbs of Maseru can still have a very rural feel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Maseru-Mafeteng road
metas.note: The section of the A2 between Maseru and Mafeteng has by far the best road quality in all of Lesotho.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Qacha's Nek
metas.note:
Qacha's Nek is a very recognizable town that is located far away from most other towns, on the southeastern border with South Africa.

It is situated right in the middle of green mountains, and it had noticeably bad weather when the Google car drove there.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Ramatsediso-Sehlabathebe NP road
metas.note:
The road going from Ramatsediso to Sehlabathebe NP, in the southeast on the border with South Africa, is very recognizable. Consider guessing there if the following three things are all true for your location:

  • Unpaved road with light brown soil.
  • Good weather with little fluffy clouds.
  • Grassy landscape high in the mountains.

You will also often be able to see exposed, light-coloured rocks next to the road.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Section of the A25
metas.note: On a section of the A25, just east of the big reservoir, the camera is covered in raindrops in one direction.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lesotho - Water reservoirs
metas.note:
There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections.

The larger Katse reservoir is visible from parts of the A25. The smaller Mohale reservoir is visible from an off-road of the A3.

NOTE: Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Nigeria - A121
metas.note:
The A121 can be recognized by the lush, tropical vegetation surrounding the divided highway, with a short, concrete median. Being a major highway, many vehicles, especially trucks, can be seen along it.

NOTE: The A232 heading east of Benin City is also divided, however the median is noticeably wider than that of the A121.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - A3 Yobe State
metas.note: The A3 going east of Potiskum to the Borno State border can be recognized by the Generation 4 coverage, mostly open arid landscape, and the highway being divided.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Blue shitcam
metas.note: This variant of shitcam with a distinct blue tint can be found in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Dark red soil
metas.note:
Dark red soil is most commonly found in and around Benin City and Enugu.

NOTE: Red-tinged soil can be found in many places. This tip refers specifically to dark red soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - East of Lekki
metas.note: A flat landscape with coastal vegetation and many palms can be seen east of Lekki. The ground is very sandy. Almost all of the coverage is old Generation 3, with a silver follow car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Obudu Plateau
metas.note: The Obudu Plateau road can be recognized by having the tallest mountains in Nigeria with street view coverage. The road winds up lush, green mountains and the coverage is slightly foggy and wet.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Old generation 3 follow car
metas.note:
This map shows where each old Generation 3 follow car can be found. They are uncommon, but can still be useful to know.

NOTE: The A121 is not shown on the map as it is recognizable from other clues. This silver Lexus, not shown on the map, can rarely be seen on the highway between Onitsha and Enugu.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Nigeria - Takum-Jalingo road
metas.note:
A dry, hazy, and somewhat gloomy landscape in Generation 3 combined with sizable mountains in the distance can be found on the road heading north of Takum to Jalingo. This smudge, which gets darker further north, is also seen at the front of the camera.

NOTE: The coverage is broken on many parts of the road, so knowing where coverage exists can be helpful.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/nigeria.

metas.name: Reunion - Bollards
metas.note: The two largest towns in Réunion can be differentiated by their bollards, commonly seen at intersections. Saint Paul uses black bollards, while Saint Denis uses green bollards, often with white balls on top. Saint Denis is also more built up, being the capital.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Reunion - Eastern part of the N2
metas.note: The eastern region of Réunion is the least densely populated, evident by the eastern part of the N2, which is a single carriageway passing through somewhat dense vegetation on both sides, or a vast landscape with little to no trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Reunion - La Route Forestière 58
metas.note: La Route Forestière 58 de la Scierie et du Haut des Makes is a winding dirt track that can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding it, particularly pine trees and eucalyptus. The track itself is also dark in colour, with grass growing in the middle of it.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Reunion - Northwestern section of the N1
metas.note:
The northwestern section of the N1 is divided, with a distinct ridge to the southeast and the ocean to the northwest.

Note that although a bridge appears on the map, the coverage was taken before the bridge was built, meaning you will not see the bridge.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Reunion - Route du Volcan
metas.note: Route du Volcan can be recognized by the Martian landscape. The only vegetation is scattered shrubs and the soil is a distinct brown-red colour. These white stones lining the road are also a good clue.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Rwanda - Big River
metas.note: A wide river (Nyabugogo) can be seen along the northeastern border of Kigali City.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - Butare
metas.note: Many roads in Butare feature cobblestone pavement.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - Kigali
metas.note: Much of the Kigali coverage is in the richer neighbourhoods. You will see a lot of luxury villas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - NR11 north of Mabanza
metas.note: The NR11 north of Mabanza uses all white road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - NR15 from Muhanga till the Western Province border
metas.note: The section of NR15 from Muhanga till the Western Province border has very poor pavement, with a lot of potholes and a lack of road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - NR15 from the Western Province border to a point 22 km west
metas.note:
The section of NR15 from the Western Province border to this point is under construction, with no pavement at the moment; making it the only covered National Road to be unpaved for this long. Also, most of the road hugs a steep cliffside made of red dirt.

NOTE: Non-national roads are often unpaved, but they are usually not as wide, and have more stuff going on around them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: Rwanda - Nyungwe Forest National Park
metas.note:
The Nyungwe Forest National Park goes through a lush and hilly landscape, which has 2 distinct covered roads; The yellow NR10 is paved, with roadlines. French style bollards and green lamp posts can be seen on the sides of the road. The white NR26 going south is mostly paved, except for the southernmost section. No roadlines are present.

This coverage was taken with the brown Google car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/rwanda.

metas.name: SA - Cape Town mountain
metas.note: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - Durban lamp
metas.note: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this bump on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - George mountain
metas.note: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - Johannesburg dodgy adverts
metas.note: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with dodgy adverts for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - Johannesburg three strips
metas.note: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of reflective tape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - Metropolitan Routes
metas.note:
Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M.

These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha) and Durban, respectively.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SA - R360 north of Bokspits
metas.note: The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Senegal - Antenna down
metas.note: The white Generation 4 car but with the antenna down, parallel to the car’s roof, can be found on the N6 between Ziguinchor and Kolda.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Box
metas.note: The silver Generation 4 car with a box in the back right of the cab can mainly be seen on the road between Richard Toll and Louga, and the N3 between Tiourene and Matam. It can also be seen on the dirt road hugging the Mauritanian border, from Matam to Gassamberi. Finally, it can be seen on a few roads near Diolotène.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Dakar
metas.note: Dakar is the largest and capital city of Senegal. It can be recognized by the denseness of the city and taller, more modern buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Dirty back
metas.note: The white Generation 4 car with a noticeably dirty back can be seen on the road going north of Kolda, up to Katonfara.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Dirty roof
metas.note: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left and a dirty roof can mainly be seen on the N1 between Kaffrine and Tambacounda, and the N7 between Tambacounda and Kedougou. It can also be seen between Dahra and Diakhao.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Divided highways
metas.note:
Divided highways are found between Dakar and Touba. The two divided highways are between Dakar and Touba, and between Dakar and Saly.

NOTE: On Google Maps, the road shows as a yellow road but without road number. There are also no divided highways in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Forest of Thies road
metas.note: The white road in the Forest of Thies can be recognized by the dry, slightly hilly landscape with brown vegetation. The road itself is made of bright orange dirt. There is also a noticeably haze in the coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Great Mosque of Touba
metas.note: The infamous Great Mosque of Touba can be recognized by the five tall minarets, which can be seen from afar.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Hazy coverage
metas.note: Hazy coverage with a low sun through a sometimes agricultural landscape can be seen on the N2 between St. Louis and Richard Toll.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Kedougou-Malian border road
metas.note:
The road northeast of Kedougou to the Malian border can be recognized by the hazy bushfire coverage. Smoke trails can sometimes be seen in the distance. The road is paved south of Saraya.

NOTE: The car is always blurred.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Kola-Velingara road
metas.note: The Kola-Velingara road between Saré Amirou and Badion is a dirt road that can be recognized by the late afternoon to evening coverage. The coverage gets later toward the west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Left stain
metas.note: The silver Generation 4 car with a stain at the back left of the cab can be seen on the N2 from Richard Toll to Matam and Bakel to Nayé. It can also be seen on the N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé
metas.note: The N1 between Tambacounda and Nayé generally runs in a northeast east direction. A railway runs parallel to the road. The railway is to the south of the road between Tambacounda to just before Youpe Amadi, and is to the north from Youpe Amadi to Bellé.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - N2 between Richard Toll and Matam
metas.note:
The N2 between Richard Toll and Matam is a wide road going through a flat desert landscape with very sparse trees. It can be recognized by the bright blue skies with no clouds. The road itself goes east-west and northeast-southwest.

NOTE: The higher the sun is, the more east you are.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - N3
metas.note: Distinct, tall patches of bright yellow grass can be seen along the N3, mostly to the east in the Matam Region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Red cloth
metas.note: The silver Generation 4 car with a red cloth at the front left can be seen on this eastern road between Ouro Sogui and Bakel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Senegal - Saloum River Delta
metas.note: A flat, slightly marshy landscape with low vegetation can be seen on a few sections of roads in the Saloum River Delta.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: Southwestern Portugal
metas.note: In the far southwest of the country you can find a flat uncultivated landscape with very limited vegetation, which typically appears quite dry. There are almost no trees nearby, and only very low bushes and grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: SP - Trinidade pole
metas.note: The town of Trinidade has poles with red and white pole paint.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.

metas.name: Tunisia - Bizerte Lake
metas.note: Bizerte Lake is instantly recognizable due to its teal coloured waters. There are slight hills to its south, with the rest of the area around the lake being flat. The city of Bizerte is located on the northeast side of the lake.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Caseway
metas.note: You can easily recognise the Djerba-Zarzis causeway thanks to the water on both sides and the pipeline that is always present to your west.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Gabes
metas.note:
If you see a large amount of palm trees in a single place, you are probably in Gabes.

NOTE: While Djerba also has many palm trees, the towns and surrounding area tend to look more rural.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - P1 sandy hills
metas.note: On the P1 road northwest of Medinine, you can occasionally find sandy hills that look like this. These hills are quite unique, as most coverage in southern Tunisia is in very flat areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Sahli offroad
metas.note: An offroad from road P12 southwest of Sousse can be recognised by the dark pavement surrounded by bright sandy soil combined with the east-west road angle. The eastern part of the road is fairly vegetated, with large numbers of prickly pears, while the western part of the road is very arid with little to no vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Tunisia - Trekkers
metas.note: Trekkers can be found all over the country, even in places far away from the area with car coverage. Coverage includes archaeological sites, forts, mosques, and a Star Wars set, among other things.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.
